G18.boundary: native CLI workload evidence only; not GPU evidence

acceptance.check: Actual Chrome on M4 requests a WebGPU adapter/device, compiles the owned WGSL shader, renders the bounded scene, and supports pointer object selection and keyboard/button movement; no benchmark claim.
Missing WebGPU/adapter and a controlled GPUDevice.lost fixture produce stable accessible UNSUPPORTED/DEVICE_LOST states, disable controls, and never silently fall back to CPU/WebGL.

Rust HTTP tests cover the canvas/module/WGSL routes and CSP/MIME; dependency-free Node fixtures cover adapter absence, pointer mapping, bounded movement and device loss; existing task-console behavior stays intact. Static asset GETs do not allocate extra console sessions.

Exact core AGENTS commands, native Rust fmt/clippy/tests/build, selected portable Wasm, Node fixtures, translation fingerprint, diff checks, exact-head CI/review, post-merge main CI and pinned workspace check pass.

hardware.webgpu_adapter: requestAdapter and requestDevice succeeded in actual Chrome; adapter identity was not collected

local.unittest: passed; 47 tests, includes Node state fixtures

local.rust_check: passed; native fmt, clippy -D warnings, full workspace tests/build, selected contracts/platform Wasm build and dependency inventory
local.node_fixtures: passed; Node v26.11.1, 5 tests including moved-object hit mapping and loss-during-initialization guard
local.actual_chrome: passed; 2026-10-12, Google Chrome 154.0.8037.98 on Apple M4 Pro/macOS 27.0.1; served only from http://127.0.0.1; WebGPU ready, three cubes visibly rendered, pointer selected object 3, Right moved selected cube; no external site opened; temporary local service stopped gracefully

GPUDevice loss can occur during initialization or after rendering; controls must remain disabled after loss.
WGSL shader and Canvas WebGPU context are explicit browser platform dependencies.
